After two decades of Napoleonic wars, Europe's great powers sat down in Vienna to redraw the continent. Here is the result in 1816.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The Congress of Vienna ran from September 1814 to June 1815. Metternich chaired for Austria, Castlereagh spoke for Britain, Talleyrand for defeated France. The Final Act was signed on 9 June 1815, nine days before Waterloo.
2/ Germany: about 300 states of the old Holy Roman Empire were consolidated into a German Confederation of 39 states, presided over by Austria. That is the dashed line on the map.
3/ The Netherlands and the former Southern Netherlands (roughly modern Belgium) were joined under the House of Orange-Nassau. The union lasted until Belgium broke away in 1830.

4/ Russia got most of the Duchy of Warsaw as a Kingdom of Poland under the Tsar. Prussia gained about three-fifths of Saxony plus territory in the Rhineland and Westphalia, hence the western Prussian pieces on the map.
5/ Norway passed from Denmark to Sweden under the Treaty of Kiel, creating Sweden-Norway. Switzerland's neutrality was guaranteed.
6/ Many historians credit the settlement with helping Europe avoid a continent-wide war for decades. Others say it simply froze tensions that nationalism later broke open.
Which border on this map aged the worst? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
